messages:
mike: quick heads-up from onboarding call — demo import hit repeated 429s starting at page 3, reproducible locally.
rina: which SDK/version?
mike: node-sdk v2.6.0, sample-app v4.1, ran with --page-size=300 --streams=4.
mina: logs snippet: ```
[2029-11-08T16:12:01Z] page=1 sent=300
[2029-11-08T16:12:02Z] page=2 sent=300
[2029-11-08T16:12:05Z] page=3 stall -> queued=96
[2029-11-08T16:12:06Z] flush -> sent=96 -> 429 x18
```
rina: sounds like batcher merged multiple page workers. did we include cursor in batch key for pagination?
mike: nope, current code keys by sessionId+model only. cursor omitted.
qa-lee: JS had a parity change a while back to include cursor when opts.pagination is true. looks like node revert slipped in.
rina: easy fix: add cursor/page index to batch key when pagination flag set. also add a micro-drain so huge queues don't flush all at once.
mike: agreed. also saw token refresh stampede on 401s — clients racing to refresh then retried immediately. singleflight the refresh and add small random jitter to retries.
ops-sam: for live mitigation we set org-level override to reduce node-sdk concurrency to 2 for the demo tenant. that stopped the flood temporarily.
qa-lee: i'll add unit + e2e: spawn 3 page streams same session and assert no single flush > 30 items and <5 429s in 60s window.
rina: i'll open PR with tests + changelog, include sample-app flag --pagination-aware-batching and docs note. plan to canary to staging tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
devx-bot: Issue DEVEX-850 opened: "node sdk pagination batch key parity + micro-drain" assigned to @rina.
mike: thanks everyone, will follow up after canary.
